places.name: Athens
places.clue: The marble Parthenon has crowned its Acropolis hill since the 5th century BCE.

places.name: Santorini
places.clue: Its whitewashed villages cling to the rim of a flooded caldera left by a colossal Bronze Age eruption.

places.name: Thessaloniki
places.clue: Greece's second city was the birthplace of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, founder of modern Turkey.

places.name: Meteora
places.clue: Monks built monasteries atop these towering rock pillars, once reachable only by ladders or nets hauled up by rope.

places.name: Mount Olympus
places.clue: Greece's highest peak, at about 2,918 metres, was the mythical home of the twelve Olympian gods.

places.name: Delphi
places.clue: Ancient Greeks considered this mountainside sanctuary of Apollo, home of the famous oracle, the navel of the world.

places.name: Knossos
places.clue: Legend placed the Minotaur's labyrinth in this sprawling Bronze Age palace of the Minoans on Crete.

places.name: Olympia
places.clue: This sanctuary of Zeus hosted the ancient Olympic Games, and the modern Olympic flame is still lit here.

places.name: Corfu
places.clue: Venice held this Ionian island for four centuries, and Ottoman sieges never managed to capture it.

places.name: Mystras
places.clue: This hillside Byzantine city near Sparta was among the last great centres of Byzantine learning.

places.name: Mount Athos
places.clue: Twenty Orthodox monasteries share this peninsula, where women have been barred from setting foot for about a thousand years.

places.name: Vikos Gorge
places.clue: Guinness World Records once listed this Epirus canyon as the world's deepest gorge in proportion to its width.
